gates.name: Run tests
gates.detail: 492 tests, 484 pass, 3 fail, 5 skipped (node --test, full suite via `npm test`, Windows). All three failures are file-level synthetic entries — dist/records/index.test.js, dist/session-manager/index.test.js, dist/store/index.test.js — each wrapping the identical pre-existing error: 'Error: A resource generated asynchronous activity after the test ended. This activity created the error "Error: A FileHandle object was closed during garbage collection. This used to be allowed with a deprecation warning but is now considered an error. Please close FileHandle objects explicitly." which triggered an uncaughtException event, caught by the test runner.' No individual named assertion failed inside any of the three files (confirmed by re-running dist/records/index.test.js in isolation: 25/26 pass, the sole 'failure' being the same file-level GC wrapper with zero failing assertions). This matches issue #292, 'npm test intermittently reports file-level failure from an unclosed FileHandle GC warning (Windows)', already filed and open before this PR. records/index.test.ts is otherwise untouched by this slice's behavioural changes (only a mechanical `as never` cast was added to its Config fixture), and the same failure reproduces identically, so this is pre-existing environment flakiness, not a regression introduced by S31.
